name: ai-maestro-janitor
description: Keeps your dev environment tidy and secure, in the background: drift + supply-chain detectors, secret/injection guards on tool calls, rate-limit auto-resume, prompt-cache keep-alive, and a markdown memory system. Runs on a per-session CronCreate heartbeat (session-scoped, re-armed each session) plus one machine-wide background daemon that owns every global-scope update.

github_repo.title: GitHub Repository
github_repo.description: GitHub repo slug for PR reconciliation (owner/repo). Defaults to the origin remote when unset.

trdd_path.title: TRDD Directory Path
trdd_path.description: Relative path from project root to the TRDD directory. Default: design/tasks

heartbeat_cron.title: Heartbeat Cron Expression
heartbeat_cron.description: Standard 5-field cron for the janitor heartbeat — the INITIAL cadence baked at /janitor-arm. Default: "*/5 * * * *". When heartbeat_cadence_dynamic is on (default), the dispatcher AUTO-TIERS from here: it writes the desired cron to .janitor/state/desired-cadence.cron and re-arms (via the [janitor-renew] marker) to a FAST/MID/SLOW cadence chosen from live state, so the fixed value here converges within 1-2 fires. Set heartbeat_cadence_dynamic=false to pin this fixed cadence and disable tiering.

keep_going_default.title: Never-stop keep-going nudge is ON by default
keep_going_default.description: When true (DEFAULT, user directive 2026-07-16), every due heartbeat emits the never-stop continue-nudge in EVERY mode — the janitor keeps an unattended fleet working in the user's absence without needing a per-session opt-in. The nudge is bounded (one line added to an already-scheduled heartbeat turn) and is silenced only by a deliberate act: the explicit `/janitor-keep-going off` sentinel (full mode only — maintenance mode always nudges and is exited via `/janitor-maintenance-mode off`). Set to false to restore the pre-2026-07-16 opt-IN behaviour: silent in full mode unless the per-session keep-going flag is set.

heartbeat_cadence_dynamic.title: Dynamic TTL-aware heartbeat cadence
heartbeat_cadence_dynamic.description: When true (DEFAULT), the dispatcher self-selects the heartbeat cadence each fire (TRDD-0QQX9H0G, issue #83): FAST=*/5 when the session is actively waiting (rate-limited, a pending resume, in-flight background agents, keep-going) — the same cadence as today, so recovery latency is unchanged; MID=*/15 on recent user activity; SLOW=*/30 (bounded by the real cache-TTL) when idle — cutting idle heartbeat cost ~6x (a measured quiet fire on a large session ≈ $0.76; */5 = 12 fires/h vs */30 = 2/h) with NO recovery regression. A tier change is applied by re-arming through the existing [janitor-renew] marker (dispatch cannot call CronCreate itself). When false, the phase is a total no-op and the fixed heartbeat_cron is used unchanged.

heartbeat_ttl_regime.title: Cache-TTL regime for cadence
heartbeat_ttl_regime.description: Which prompt-cache-TTL regime the SLOW keep-warm ceiling assumes: "auto" (DEFAULT) resolves it authoritatively via the agentlensPro get_account_status probe (see heartbeat_account_status_command), falling back to an env heuristic (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set → 5-min tier, else 60-min) when the probe is unavailable. "subscription" forces the 60-min regime (SLOW */30), "api-key" forces the 5-min regime (all tiers */5, no slowdown). Only "auto" runs the probe.

heartbeat_account_status_command.title: Account-status probe command (cadence TTL regime)
heartbeat_account_status_command.description: Shell command that prints JSON with a cacheTtl.minutes field naming the current prompt-cache TTL (e.g. AgentLens: 'agentlenspro get_account_status'). Consulted ONLY when heartbeat_ttl_regime=auto. Default: 'agentlenspro get_account_status' (a bare PATH binary). Empty string disables the probe → pure env fallback. Result is cached in .janitor/state/ttl-regime.json and re-probed only every heartbeat_regime_probe_interval seconds. Fail-open: a missing binary, non-zero exit, 5s timeout, or unparseable output falls back to the env heuristic and never blocks the fire (same contract as heartbeat_cost_command). Config, not a hard-coded path, because such CLIs are machine-local.

heartbeat_regime_probe_interval.title: Cache-TTL regime probe interval (seconds)
heartbeat_regime_probe_interval.description: Minimum seconds between account-status probes for the cadence TTL regime. Default: 1800 (30 min). The regime changes rarely (a plan/billing-mode switch), so a fresh cache is reused between probes — at most one short subprocess per interval per project.

heartbeat_cadence_demote_fires.title: Cadence demote hysteresis (fires)
heartbeat_cadence_demote_fires.description: Consecutive idle fires required before the cadence demotes to a SLOWER tier. Default: 2. Promotion to a FASTER tier is always immediate (a rate-limited session must speed up at once); only demotion waits this many fires, so a single idle fire between active ones does not flap the cron (which would trigger a needless re-arm).

heartbeat_cron_fast.title: FAST-tier cron override
heartbeat_cron_fast.description: Override the FAST-tier heartbeat cron (active-waiting sessions: rate-limited / resume-pending). Default empty = built-in "*/5 * * * *" — the same cadence as the fixed pre-#83 default, so an actively-waiting session has NO recovery-latency regression. Ignored in the fast-TTL regime, where every tier is forced to */5.

heartbeat_cron_mid.title: MID-tier cron override
heartbeat_cron_mid.description: Override the MID-tier heartbeat cron (recent-activity sessions). Default empty = built-in "*/15 * * * *" in the slow-TTL regime (3x cheaper than */5). Ignored in the fast-TTL regime.

heartbeat_cron_slow.title: SLOW-tier cron override
heartbeat_cron_slow.description: Override the SLOW-tier heartbeat cron (idle keep-warm). Default empty = built-in "*/30 * * * *" in the slow-TTL regime (2 fires/h, 30-min gaps under the 1h cache TTL with margin; 6x cheaper than */5). */30 is the safe floor for a uniform cadence — any */N with 30<=N<60 fires exactly twice an hour, so a slower uniform cron is not possible without a 60-min (at-TTL) gap. Ignored in the fast-TTL regime, where every tier is */5.

issues_watch_interval.title: GitHub issues-watch cadence (seconds)
issues_watch_interval.description: Minimum seconds between GitHub issue-tracker checks, when the watcher is enabled for a project via /janitor-issues-watch-on. The watcher is OFF by default and costs nothing until enabled. Default: 1800 (30 min) — issues do not churn every 5 minutes and each due fire costs one `gh` call.

pr_reconciler_interval.title: PR Reconciler Internal Cadence (seconds)
pr_reconciler_interval.description: Minimum seconds between PR reconciliation passes. The heartbeat may fire more often; this just throttles the detector's work. Default: 900 (15 min).

worktree_janitor_interval.title: Worktree Janitor Internal Cadence (seconds)
worktree_janitor_interval.description: Minimum seconds between worktree scans. Default: 900 (15 min).

trdd_drift_interval.title: TRDD Drift Check Internal Cadence (seconds)
trdd_drift_interval.description: Minimum seconds between TRDD drift checks. Default: 3600 (1 h).

trdd_reminder_interval.title: TRDD Reminder Internal Cadence (seconds)
trdd_reminder_interval.description: Minimum seconds between in-progress TRDD reminders. Default: 14400 (4 h).

task_pr_mismatch_interval.title: Task/PR Mismatch Internal Cadence (seconds)
task_pr_mismatch_interval.description: Minimum seconds between task/PR cross-checks. Default: 1800 (30 min).

trdd_staleness_days.title: TRDD Staleness Threshold (days)
trdd_staleness_days.description: Days a TRDD can sit 'In progress' before it counts as drift. Default: 14.

stale_pr_days.title: Stale PR Threshold (days)
stale_pr_days.description: Days an open PR can sit without new commits before it counts as stale. Default: 14.

stale_task_interval.title: Stale Task Detector Cadence (seconds)
stale_task_interval.description: Minimum seconds between stale-task scans. Default: 1800 (30 min).

stale_in_progress_threshold.title: Stale in_progress Threshold (seconds)
stale_in_progress_threshold.description: Seconds an in_progress task can sit with no update before nudging. Default: 7200 (2 h).

stale_pending_threshold.title: Stale pending Threshold (seconds)
stale_pending_threshold.description: Seconds a pending task can sit with no update before nudging. Default: 86400 (24 h).

dirty_tree_interval.title: Dirty Tree Detector Cadence (seconds)
dirty_tree_interval.description: Minimum seconds between dirty-tree checks. Default: 300 (5 min).

dirty_tree_threshold.title: Dirty Tree Threshold (seconds)
dirty_tree_threshold.description: Seconds the working tree can stay dirty before nudging to commit. Default: 1800 (30 min). Commit often — each commit is a recovery point.

subagent_report_interval.title: Subagent Report Detector Cadence (seconds)
subagent_report_interval.description: Minimum seconds between subagent-report scans. Default: 3600 (1 h).

subagent_report_lookback.title: Subagent Report Lookback Window (seconds)
subagent_report_lookback.description: Age cutoff for reports considered 'fresh' and needing action. Default: 86400 (24 h).

heartbeat_renewal_threshold_days.title: Heartbeat Auto-Renewal Threshold (days)
heartbeat_renewal_threshold_days.description: Days after arming before dispatch.py emits a [janitor-renew] nudge. Claude re-runs /janitor-arm in response, which idempotently replaces the cron before the 7-day auto-expiry. Default: 6. Lower = earlier nudge / safer. Higher = later nudge and risks missing the 7-day window if Claude is rate-limited or offline.

heartbeat_cost_command.title: Heartbeat Cost Command (opt-in)
heartbeat_cost_command.description: Full shell command of a CLI that prints ONE line with the exact token+dollar cost of the PREVIOUS heartbeat fire (e.g. AgentLens: 'node ~/Code/agentlens/scripts/agentlens-heartbeat-cost.js --oneline'). Default: empty (disabled). When set, dispatch.py runs it on every fire — full AND maintenance mode — and appends its first stdout line to .janitor/logs/heartbeat-cost.log, building a greppable per-fire cost series. It never prints to the fire's stdout (a per-fire stdout line would cost output tokens on every fire, taxing the thing it measures). Fail-open: a non-zero exit, timeout (20s), or missing binary means no line this fire; the fire is never blocked. The command is config (not a hard-coded path) because such CLIs are typically machine-local.

heartbeat_cadence_dwell_s.title: Cadence Re-arm Dwell (seconds)
heartbeat_cadence_dwell_s.description: After a heartbeat re-arm (a [janitor-renew] that changed the cadence tier), suppress further renew emissions for this many seconds UNLESS promoting to FAST for a genuine non-self signal (janitor#89 / TRDD-CI6ZTNB9). Kills the tier oscillation where the controller chased the background agents it itself spawned — each memory chore used to cost 2 wasted re-arm turns. Default 1200 (20 min); 0 disables the dwell.

token_budget_repeat_s.title: Token-Spike Nudge Repeat Interval (seconds)
token_budget_repeat_s.description: The pre-tool-token-budget hook now injects its advisory additionalContext only on a TIER TRANSITION (janitor#79 — steady-tier per-call injection was the #2 measured cause of prompt-cache re-bills). At a steady HARD tier it re-nudges after this interval so a persistent spike is not forgotten. Default 600 (10 min). Enforcement (the opt-in deny of agent spawns at the hard tier) is unaffected by this throttle.

context_prepare_renudge_s.title: Context-Usage Nudge Repeat Interval (seconds)
context_prepare_renudge_s.description: The pre-tool-context-usage hook now injects its advisory additionalContext only on a SEVERITY TRANSITION (janitor#79). While the context stays in the prepare/advisory band it re-nudges after this interval instead of on every tool call. Default 600 (10 min). The >=85% ENFORCEMENT path (auto-compact + deny) is unaffected.

heartbeat_burn_status_command.title: Burn-rate probe command (token-anomaly corroboration)
heartbeat_burn_status_command.description: Shell command that prints JSON with a global.costPerHour field naming the CURRENT machine-wide burn rate in $/hour (e.g. AgentLens: 'agentlenspro get_burn_status'). Consulted by the token-usage-anomaly detector ONLY after its local median+MAD baseline has already decided to alarm, to CORROBORATE the spike with the real account-level burn rate — it never suppresses the local alarm (the local baseline is authoritative for 'this session's own heartbeat cost spiked'). Default: 'agentlenspro get_burn_status' (a bare PATH binary). Empty string disables the probe. Fail-open: a missing binary, non-zero exit, 5s timeout, or unparseable output yields no clause and never blocks the fire (same contract as heartbeat_account_status_command). Config, not a hard-coded path, because such CLIs are machine-local.

heartbeat_investigate_burn_command.title: Burn-culprit probe command (window-burn + token-anomaly attribution)
heartbeat_investigate_burn_command.description: Shell command that prints JSON with a findings[] array naming the top burn CULPRIT and its cause (e.g. FORK_STORM), shareOfWindow and confidence, derived from real OTEL telemetry (e.g. AgentLens: 'agentlenspro investigate_burn'). Consulted ONLY on a tripped alarm by two detectors: window-burn-rate PREFERS this cause clause over its native transcript-size attribution, and token-usage-anomaly appends it as attribution. Never run speculatively (only post-trip). Default: 'agentlenspro investigate_burn' (a bare PATH binary). Empty string disables the probe, falling back to the native attribution. Fail-open: any failure yields no clause and never blocks the fire. Config, not a hard-coded path, because such CLIs are machine-local.

version_check_interval.title: Version Update Check Cadence (seconds)
version_check_interval.description: Minimum seconds between checks against api.github.com for a newer plugin release. Default: 300 (5 min — runs every heartbeat by default). The detector queries the repo declared in plugin.json's `repository` field, so forks check against their own releases. Silent on network/auth failures. The GitHub query short-circuits when nothing changed; a 5-min cadence costs ~12 cheap requests/hour, well inside both the unauthenticated (60/h) and `gh`-authenticated (5000/h) API limits.

auto_update_on_new_release.title: Auto-update on new plugin release
auto_update_on_new_release.description: When true (DEFAULT since v0.5.3), the global janitor daemon runs `claude plugin marketplace update ai-maestro-plugins` + `claude plugin update ai-maestro-janitor@ai-maestro-plugins --scope <auto-detected>` whenever a newer release is found on GitHub. On success the daemon sets reload-needed.flag → the next heartbeat emits [janitor-reload] → Claude silently runs /reload-plugins → the auto-rolling cron stub picks up the new version on the next fire. Fully autonomous; no human in the loop. When false, the version-update detector instead surfaces a manual nudge for the user to run /plugin update by hand. Single-writer semantics are guaranteed by the daemon's flock (closes issue #7). Auto-update is best-effort: any CLI failure falls back silently to the manual-nudge path.

version_update_on_release_trigger.title: Release-triggered janitor self-update
version_update_on_release_trigger.description: When true (DEFAULT), the per-session version-update detector -- on noticing the plugin cache is behind the latest GitHub release -- raises a global request flag the daemon consumes on its next loop (<= ~60 s), so a new janitor release lands in ~5-6 min instead of on the daemon's 6 h self-update beat (daemon_version_update_interval). The detector still never runs `claude plugin update` itself -- it only REQUESTS; the daemon remains the single global writer (issue #7 / PRRD S2.1). Gated additionally by auto_update_on_new_release: with that off, no request is raised. When false, self-updates fall back to the pure 6 h beat. Fail-open: any flag hiccup silently falls back to the 6 h beat.

daemon_enabled.title: Global janitor daemon enabled
daemon_enabled.description: When true (default), per-session heartbeats lazy-spawn a single OS-wide daemon (scripts/daemon.py) on ~/.claude/janitor-global-state/ that owns every machine-global auto-update task — marketplace-refresh and user-plugins-update. Singleton enforced via exclusive flock so N concurrent Claude Code sessions across N projects produce ONE worker, not N (closes issue #7). When false, the daemon is never spawned AND the per-session shims for the global tasks become silent no-ops. Manual kill switch: `touch ~/.claude/janitor-global-state/kill-switch.flag` (running daemon exits on next loop tick).

leanctx_autoallow.title: Auto-allow janitor commands in the lean-ctx shell allowlist
leanctx_autoallow.description: When true (DEFAULT), the SessionStart hook additively runs `lean-ctx allow <cmd>` for each command the janitor heartbeat needs (dispatcher-stub.py, uv, python3, git, memgrep, -d) on machines that run the lean-ctx Bash-allowlist wrapper. This self-heals the block that otherwise stops the cron's bare `dispatcher-stub.py` invocation and tempts dangerous bypasses. It is ADDITIVE and idempotent and NEVER disables shell security or redefines the allowlist; it is a silent no-op when lean-ctx is not installed. Set to false to manage the lean-ctx allowlist yourself.

ensure_settings_enabled.title: Ensure recommended Claude Code settings in ~/.claude/settings.json
ensure_settings_enabled.description: When true (DEFAULT), the SessionStart hook keeps a fixed set of recommended settings in the user-global ~/.claude/settings.json. Group A: 8 env keys (ENABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS, ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false, CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT, CLAUDE_AUTO_BACKGROUND_TASKS, CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG, CLAUDE_AFK_COUNTDOWN_MS, CLAUDE_AFK_TIMEOUT_MS, CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS) added to the env block ONLY IF MISSING (an existing value is never overwritten). Group B: askUserQuestionTimeout=60s enforced at the top level (set if missing OR different; note CLAUDE_AFK_TIMEOUT_MS=300000 overrides it to 5 min when set). Idempotent, atomic (tmp+os.replace), and fail-safe (a malformed settings.json is left untouched). settings.json is read at Claude Code startup, so changes apply on the NEXT launch, not the current session. Set to false to manage these settings yourself.

daemon_marketplace_refresh_interval.title: Daemon Marketplace Refresh Cadence (seconds)
daemon_marketplace_refresh_interval.description: Minimum seconds the daemon waits between bulk `claude plugin marketplace update` runs (no args = every configured marketplace). Default: 1200 (20 min). The daemon is the only writer of the GLOBAL refresh, so a moderate cadence is enough — there is no per-session contention to compensate for. Narrower per-session refreshes of just the local+project plugins' marketplaces still run every 5 min (see marketplace_refresh_interval), so newly-installed marketplaces in `.claude/settings.json` / `.claude/settings.local.json` reach the catalog quickly even while the daemon is between fires. Heartbeat per-session shim emits a stale-daemon drift line when the actual last-run is older than 2× this value.

daemon_user_plugins_update_interval.title: Daemon User-scope Plugins Update Cadence (seconds)
daemon_user_plugins_update_interval.description: Minimum seconds the daemon waits between full user-scope plugin sweeps. Default: 3600 (1 h). Each sweep enumerates `claude plugin list --json`, filters to scope==user, and runs `claude plugin update <id> --scope user` sequentially per plugin. Hourly is the right balance for ~80 plugins × ~5 s each (~7 min per sweep) — fresh enough without burning CPU. The per-session shim emits a stale-daemon drift line when the actual last-run is older than 2× this value.

daemon_version_update_interval.title: Daemon Janitor-Self-Update Cadence (seconds)
daemon_version_update_interval.description: Minimum seconds the daemon waits between janitor self-update checks. Default: 21600 (6 h). Each cycle reads the local cache's highest installed version, queries the latest GitHub release of the plugin repo (via `gh api releases/latest`), and — when behind — runs `claude plugin update ai-maestro-janitor@ai-maestro-plugins --scope <auto-detected>` per discovered scope. GitHub releases land at human-day granularity so 6 h cadence keeps everything fresh without churning the network. Gated additionally by auto_update_on_new_release — when that knob is false this cycle is a no-op.

trashcan_purge_enabled.title: Trashcan auto-purge enabled
trashcan_purge_enabled.description: When true (default), the trashcan-purge detector auto-removes timestamped batches in <project_root>/.trashcan/ whose age exceeds trashcan_max_age_days. When false, batches accumulate indefinitely until cleared by hand. Age is computed from the folder-name timestamp (YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS±HHMM), not file mtimes — touching a file inside an old batch does not extend its life.

trashcan_max_age_days.title: Trashcan Max Age (days)
trashcan_max_age_days.description: Auto-purge threshold for safe-delete batches in .trashcan/. Default: 90. Batches whose folder-name timestamp is older than this are removed in full (folder + sibling .txt manifest). Markers (.gitkeep, README.txt) are never touched.

trashcan_purge_interval.title: Trashcan Purge Cadence (seconds)
trashcan_purge_interval.description: Minimum seconds between trashcan-purge passes. Default: 86400 (24 h). Lower values waste cycles since the threshold is measured in days.

screenshot_purge_enabled.title: Screenshot auto-purge enabled
screenshot_purge_enabled.description: When true (default), the screenshot-purge detector removes browser-UI test screenshots from <project_root>/reports/screenshots/ that exceed screenshot_max_age_hours, AND when free disk space drops below screenshot_lowdisk_min_free_gb it deletes the oldest screenshots first until free space recovers above screenshot_lowdisk_target_free_gb. Only files with screenshot extensions (.png .jpg .jpeg .webp .gif) inside reports/screenshots/ are touched — anything else (including .gitkeep, README files, and the directory itself) is left alone. The folder is gitignored per the reports rule, so screenshots are short-lived cache; bypassing safe-delete is correct here.

screenshot_max_age_hours.title: Screenshot Max Age (hours)
screenshot_max_age_hours.description: Hours a screenshot can live in reports/screenshots/ before screenshot-purge removes it. Default: 72 (3 days). Age is computed from file mtime — test runners that re-screenshot the same name reset the clock automatically.

rate_limit_flag_max_age_hours.title: Stale Rate-Limit Flag Max Age (hours)
rate_limit_flag_max_age_hours.description: Hours a project's .janitor/state/rate-limited.flag may sit untouched before the global daemon sweeps it. Default: 24. Only dispatch.py clears the flag and dispatch needs a live heartbeat cron, so a project whose cron died can never clear its own — and a stale flag makes the fleet guardian read a merely-quiet session as 'frozen' (which escalates toward a force-restart) instead of 'cron_dead' (a gentle re-arm). The StopFailure hook touches the flag on every turn-ending API error, so a genuinely rate-limited session keeps its flag fresh and is never swept. Set to 0 to disable the sweep.

screenshot_lowdisk_min_free_gb.title: Screenshot Low-Disk Trigger (GiB)
screenshot_lowdisk_min_free_gb.description: When free space on the disk holding reports/screenshots/ drops below this many GiB, screenshot-purge enters low-disk mode and deletes oldest screenshots first (regardless of age) until free space recovers above screenshot_lowdisk_target_free_gb. Default: 5. Set to 0 to disable low-disk override (age-only mode).

screenshot_lowdisk_target_free_gb.title: Screenshot Low-Disk Recovery Target (GiB)
screenshot_lowdisk_target_free_gb.description: Free-space target screenshot-purge tries to reach during a low-disk pass. Default: 10. The min/target hysteresis (5 → 10 GiB) prevents the detector from oscillating right at the threshold. If misconfigured to ≤ min_free_gb, the detector forces a 1 GiB gap at runtime.

screenshot_purge_interval.title: Screenshot Purge Cadence (seconds)
screenshot_purge_interval.description: Minimum seconds between screenshot-purge passes. Default: 3600 (1 h). With a 72 h default age threshold, hourly is the right balance — fast enough to catch newly-expired files and low-disk events, slow enough to be effectively free on idle projects.

stash_stale_days.title: Stale Stash Threshold (days)
stash_stale_days.description: Days a git stash can sit untouched before stale-stash flags it. Default: 30. Stashes are typically forgotten WIP — surfacing them on a 30-day cadence catches lost work without spamming on the same day a stash was created.

stale_stash_interval.title: Stale Stash Detector Cadence (seconds)
stale_stash_interval.description: Minimum seconds between stale-stash scans. Default: 86400 (24 h). The threshold is measured in days, so finer granularity wastes heartbeats.

remote_credentials_interval.title: Remote Credentials Detector Cadence (seconds)
remote_credentials_interval.description: Minimum seconds between remote-credentials checks. Default: 3600 (1 h). The detector is cheap (single git remote -v parse) but the failure mode (credential leak) is severe enough to want a relatively fast cadence.

nested_git_safety_interval.title: Nested Git Safety Detector Cadence (seconds)
nested_git_safety_interval.description: Minimum seconds between nested-.git scans. Default: 3600 (1 h). The check is depth-limited (mindepth 2 maxdepth 4) and prunes node_modules / .trashcan, so it stays well under the 10s detector budget on typical projects.

tracked_ignored_interval.title: Tracked-Ignored Detector Cadence (seconds)
tracked_ignored_interval.description: Minimum seconds between tracked-ignored scans. Default: 3600 (1 h). The detector is HEAD-cached: it only re-shells `git ls-files` when HEAD has moved since the last check, so this interval mainly bounds the worst case after many commits.

log_retention_days.title: Log Retention (days)
log_retention_days.description: Days of .janitor/logs/<detector>.log history to keep. Default: 30. Files older than this are pruned at most once per UTC day at the top of dispatch.py. Set to 0 to disable retention entirely (logs grow unbounded — only useful for short-lived debugging).

plugin_auto_update_enabled.title: Plugin Auto-Update Enabled
plugin_auto_update_enabled.description: When true (default), the plugin-updates detector runs `claude plugin update <id> --scope <scope>` for every project/local-scoped plugin where the marketplace manifest reports a newer version, AND (per plugin_auto_update_user_scope) enqueues a daemon request for every behind user-scope plugin. When false, the detector only emits an informational drift line and the user runs the update manually. The janitor's own plugin (ai-maestro-janitor) is always handled by version-update, never by this detector.

plugin_auto_update_user_scope.title: Plugin Auto-Update: User Scope (via daemon)
plugin_auto_update_user_scope.description: When true (default), the plugin-updates detector ALSO monitors user-scope (`~/.claude/settings.json`) enabled plugins each heartbeat and, for any behind its marketplace version, ENQUEUES a request the global daemon consumes and runs as `claude plugin update <id> --scope user` (TRDD-YMTUPQER). The detector NEVER runs the user-scope update itself — the daemon is the single global writer, so N Claude sessions across N projects do not stampede the same command (issue #7). The ai-maestro fleet plugins (maintainer/orchestrator/CPV/etc.) are EXCLUDED from this path in both the detector and the daemon — they update in lockstep on the daemon's coordinated beat to avoid fleet version skew (TRDD-db169d9e). The janitor itself fast-updates via the release-triggered self-update path (TRDD-Y9KM5RCJ). Set false to restore the previous project/local-only behavior (user-scope then only via the daemon's slower 1 h sweep). Requires plugin_auto_update_enabled.

plugin_auto_update_scopes.title: Plugin Auto-Update Scopes
plugin_auto_update_scopes.description: Comma-separated list of project-scoped plugin scopes the auto-updater will touch. Default: "local,project". The janitor distinguishes Claude Code's four scopes (managed, project, local, user — see https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings.md): `project` = `.claude/settings.json` (committed to the repo, shared with the team), `local` = `.claude/settings.local.json` (gitignored, your personal overrides for THIS project on THIS machine). This setting governs ONLY the scopes the detector updates DIRECTLY (per-session). The janitor never DIRECTLY runs a `user`-scope update from a session (single writer, issue #7) — user-scope is instead handled via the daemon-signal path (see plugin_auto_update_user_scope) — and never touches `managed` (admin-deployed) at all. `local`/`project` plugins are also filtered to those whose `projectPath` matches the current project, so a janitor running in project A will not touch project B's installs. Set to just "local" to skip the team-shared `.claude/settings.json` updates and only act on your personal `.claude/settings.local.json`.

plugin_auto_update_exclude.title: Plugin Auto-Update Exclude List
plugin_auto_update_exclude.description: Comma-separated list of `plugin@marketplace` IDs that the auto-updater will skip entirely. Use this to pin specific plugins to their current version (e.g. when a known-good version exists and a newer release has a regression). Example: "foo-plugin@some-marketplace,bar@another". Empty by default — every plugin (except ai-maestro-janitor itself) is eligible.

plugin_updates_interval.title: Plugin Updates Detector Cadence (seconds)
plugin_updates_interval.description: Minimum seconds between plugin-updates passes. Default: 300 (5 min — runs every heartbeat by default). Each fire refreshes every marketplace that has an installed plugin (one `claude plugin marketplace update` call per marketplace) and then attempts an update for each plugin where the manifest version exceeds the installed one. The marketplace refresh and per-plugin update are both cheap idempotent shell commands that no-op when nothing has changed, so a 5-minute cadence keeps every installed plugin in sync with at most a 5-minute lag while costing a few subprocess invocations per heartbeat when there is no work to do.

marketplace_refresh_interval.title: Per-Session Local+Project Marketplace Refresh Cadence (seconds)
marketplace_refresh_interval.description: Minimum seconds between per-session marketplace refreshes. Default: 300 (5 min — runs every heartbeat). Scoped: refreshes ONLY the marketplaces hosting plugins enabled in `<project>/.claude/settings.local.json` (local scope) and `<project>/.claude/settings.json` (project scope). Global / user-scope marketplaces are owned by the central daemon (see daemon_marketplace_refresh_interval, default 20 min) — the per-session detector deliberately stays narrow so N concurrent Claude Code sessions across N projects do not pile up overlapping bulk refreshes (the bug GitHub issue #7 documented). Spawns `claude plugin marketplace update <name>` once per unique marketplace, sequentially, in a detached background worker. The worker PID is tracked so successive heartbeats that find a prior worker alive skip cleanly. Also keeps the daemon-staleness watchdog (drift line when the daemon’s own refresh hasn’t finished for >2× its cadence).

user_plugins_update_interval.title: User-scope Plugins Auto-Update Cadence (seconds)
user_plugins_update_interval.description: Minimum seconds between user-plugins-update passes. Default: 300 (5 min — runs every heartbeat by default). This is Track 1 of the auto-update directive: keep every user-scope plugin fresh, project-agnostically. Each pass enumerates `claude plugin list --json` (scope=user, all plugins regardless of enabled state), then spawns a detached worker that runs `claude plugin update <id> --scope user` per plugin sequentially. The worker PID is tracked in `.janitor/state/user-plugins-update.pid`; successive heartbeats that find the prior worker still alive skip and exit, so long sweeps never pile up. Updates apply to disabled plugins too so re-enabling one uses the latest cached version. Silent on stdout — pure background maintenance.

local_plugins_update_interval.title: Local-scope Plugins Auto-Update Cadence (seconds)
local_plugins_update_interval.description: Minimum seconds between local-plugins-update passes. Default: 300 (5 min — runs every heartbeat by default). This is Track 2a of the auto-update directive: keep local-scope plugins enabled in `<project>/.claude/settings.local.json` (gitignored, personal overrides for this project) fresh. Each pass reads settings.local.json, filters `enabledPlugins` to entries with value=true (only those enabled locally), then spawns a detached worker that runs `claude plugin update <id> --scope local` per plugin. The worker PID is tracked so overlapping fires skip cleanly. Bails in <100ms when settings.local.json doesn't exist (most projects). Per-project: a janitor armed in project A only updates project A's local-scope plugins. No git mutation (settings.local.json is gitignored). Silent on stdout.

project_plugins_update_interval.title: Project-scope Plugins Auto-Update Cadence (seconds)
project_plugins_update_interval.description: Minimum seconds between project-plugins-update passes. Default: 300 (5 min — runs every heartbeat by default). This is Track 2b of the auto-update directive: keep project-scope plugins enabled in `<project>/.claude/settings.json` (git-tracked, team-shared) fresh. Each pass reads settings.json, filters `enabledPlugins` to entries with value=true, then spawns a detached worker that runs `claude plugin update <id> --scope project` per plugin. After the sweep, if `.claude/settings.json` is now dirty in git, the worker writes a commit-pending sentinel; the next heartbeat's parent run reads the sentinel and emits a `[project-plugins-commit-needed]` drift line containing the EXACT `git commit --only -- .claude/settings.json -m ...` command for Claude to execute. Signing, pre-commit hooks, and branch protection rules are honored automatically because the commit uses porcelain `git commit` with the user's git config. Whitelist is enforced: ONLY `.claude/settings.json` is ever named in the drift line — the user's other staged/unstaged files are untouched.

mcp_config_drift_interval.title: MCP Config Drift Detector Cadence (seconds)
mcp_config_drift_interval.description: Minimum seconds between mcp-config-drift passes. Default: 3600 (1 h). The detector inspects `<project>/.mcp.json` (project-scope MCP) and `~/.claude.json` `.projects[<root>].mcpServers` (local-scope MCP for THIS project only). Checks: (a) invalid JSON; (b) `.mcp.json` ambiguous tracking status (neither git-tracked nor gitignored); (c) per-server problems: missing transport, unset `$VAR`/`${VAR}` env-var references. Never inspects user-scope MCP (top-level `~/.claude.json` `.mcpServers`).

settings_scope_drift_interval.title: Settings Scope Drift Detector Cadence (seconds)
settings_scope_drift_interval.description: Minimum seconds between settings-scope-drift passes. Default: 3600 (1 h). The detector flags `.claude/settings.json` that is gitignored (project-scope settings won't reach the team) and `.claude/settings.local.json` that is git-tracked (personal local-scope settings leak to the team). Ambiguous tracking status is also flagged. Cheap — just two `git check-ignore` calls.

subagent_scope_drift_interval.title: Subagent Scope Drift Detector Cadence (seconds)
subagent_scope_drift_interval.description: Minimum seconds between subagent-scope-drift passes. Default: 3600 (1 h). The detector walks `.claude/agents/**/*.md` and flags any agent file that is neither git-tracked nor gitignored. Subagents have no formal local scope, so the git status IS the scope signal: tracked → project (team-shared), gitignored → personal. Findings are batched into a single drift line listing the first 5 + a count.

claude_md_scope_drift_interval.title: CLAUDE.md Scope Drift Detector Cadence (seconds)
claude_md_scope_drift_interval.description: Minimum seconds between claude-md-scope-drift passes. Default: 3600 (1 h). The detector flags `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/CLAUDE.md` that are gitignored (project memory should be tracked, team-shared) and `CLAUDE.local.md` that is git-tracked (personal memory should be gitignored). Ambiguous tracking status is also flagged.

cross_scope_reference_drift_interval.title: Cross-Scope Reference Drift Detector Cadence (seconds)
cross_scope_reference_drift_interval.description: Minimum seconds between cross-scope-reference-drift passes. Default: 3600 (1 h). The detector catches the silent-clone-break bug: a tracked file (agent, skill, command, CLAUDE.md) that references `/<name>` or `Skill('<name>')` whose definition resolves to a project-local file that is GITIGNORED or has AMBIGUOUS tracking. On clone, the source ships but the target doesn't, so the reference dangles. Cost: a few `grep` calls per tracked source plus one `scope_tracking_status` per resolved reference; bounded by the number of tracked agents + skills + commands.

workflow_security_enabled.title: Workflow Security Scan Enabled
workflow_security_enabled.description: When true (default), the workflow-security detector runs the janitor's native Sentinel scanner (regex + structural + repo tiers) over .github/workflows/ on every heartbeat and surfaces NEW CRITICAL/HIGH findings as a single drift line pointing to /janitor-github-workflow-doctor. READ-ONLY — it never edits a workflow or calls the GitHub API. Set false to disable heartbeat workflow scanning (the on-demand /janitor-github-workflow-doctor skill still works).

workflow_security_interval.title: Workflow Security Scan Cadence (seconds)
workflow_security_interval.description: Minimum seconds between workflow-security scans. Default: 300 (5 min — runs every heartbeat). The detector content-hashes all workflow files and returns immediately when nothing changed, so an unchanged-workflows fire costs only a few small file reads; a workflow edit forces a fresh scan and re-surfaces the current CRITICAL/HIGH set within one cadence, so a newly-introduced injection or secret-leak cannot sit unnoticed.

keychain_health_enabled.title: Keychain Health Check Enabled
keychain_health_enabled.description: When true (default, macOS only), the keychain-health detector verifies that THIS shell's macOS security session can actually reach the keychain, and surfaces a CRITICAL drift line when it cannot. It catches the 2026-07-12 fleet outage: a long-lived tmux/terminal server that survives a securityd recycle hands every pane it forks a DEAD security session, in which the Keychain Services API fails outright — so Claude Code there cannot read its OAuth item and EVERY agent reports 'Not logged in' while the credential is perfectly fine (re-running /login does NOT help). It also flags a DANGLING keychain search-list entry (a registered keychain whose file is gone — typically left by a custom-keychain tool such as `dotenclave unlock` calling `security list-keychains -s`), which is the root cause that poisons every lookup in the session. STRICTLY read-only and prompt-safe: it checks FINDABILITY only and NEVER reads a secret (no `-w`), because the secret read is what triggers the macOS ACL prompt flood; every call is routed through the mandated safe-keychain choke point (hard timeout + one-shot denied-latch). Set false to disable.

keychain_health_interval.title: Keychain Health Check Cadence (seconds)
keychain_health_interval.description: Minimum seconds between keychain-health checks. Default: 900 (15 min). A broken security session is a FLEET-DOWN condition — every agent in it is unusable — so it must surface fast, and the probe is only two cheap read-only `security` calls. The verdict is deduped (code + evidence), so a persistent breakage nags once rather than every fire, while a NEW or changed condition always surfaces.

oauth_beacon_refresh_enabled.title: OAuth Live-Identity Beacon Refresh Enabled
oauth_beacon_refresh_enabled.description: When true (default), the oauth-beacon-refresh detector keeps the OAuth rotator's live-identity beacon fresh, so proactive rotation evaluates the account that is ACTUALLY live. It is opt-in by presence: a silent no-op unless a configured rotator home exists. Why it is needed: the beacon can only be stamped from a context that can READ the primary credential, and the global daemon is headless by design (a `-w` secret read there could only raise a GUI prompt nobody can answer), so the daemon can never stamp it — leaving SessionStart as the only automatic stamp, once per session. A manual /login mid-session then left the beacon fresh-but-WRONG for up to 24h, and rotation evaluated the OLD account's usage (always 'within limits') while the real one burned to its cap. Prompt-safe: a NON-prompting attribute read (mdat, never `-w`) gates the stamp, so the steady state costs one cheap metadata call and ZERO secret reads. Set false to disable.

oauth_beacon_refresh_interval.title: OAuth Beacon Refresh Cadence (seconds)
oauth_beacon_refresh_interval.description: Minimum seconds between live-identity beacon freshness checks. Default: 300 (every heartbeat fire). This bounds how long rotation can watch a stale account after a manual /login. It is affordable at every fire because the check is gated by a non-prompting `mdat` attribute read: when the credential has not changed, nothing else runs.

branch_protection_enabled.title: Branch Protection Check Enabled
branch_protection_enabled.description: When true (default), the branch-protection detector asks the GitHub API (read-only) whether the default branch is covered by classic branch protection OR an active branch ruleset (inherited org/enterprise rulesets count), and surfaces an URGENT drift line only when it can DEFINITIVELY confirm neither is present. It NEVER configures protection itself. Skips silently when gh is absent/unauthenticated, the viewer is not a repo admin, the repo has no GitHub remote, or any probe is indeterminate. Set false to disable.

branch_protection_interval.title: Branch Protection Check Cadence (seconds)
branch_protection_interval.description: Minimum seconds between branch-protection checks. Default: 21600 (6 h). Branch rulesets change rarely and each pass makes a few gh API calls, so a slow cadence is correct; the detector nags once until fixed (seen-file dedupe) and re-arms automatically (emit_forget) if protection is later removed so a regression re-alerts.

github_config_audit_enabled.title: Fleet GitHub-Config Audit Enabled (daemon)
github_config_audit_enabled.description: ON by default (TRDD-157OH2D7). The global daemon runs a fleet-wide, READ-ONLY GitHub-config audit across every ai-maestro plugin repo (enumerated from the marketplace catalog) and writes the findings to a file the near-free per-session fleet-github-config detector surfaces. It catches what the per-session branch-protection check structurally cannot: a DIFFERENT plugin's repo left UNPROTECTED (open to stranger PRs/force-pushes), a repo carrying required_linear_history (which BLOCKS Claude's merges), or a missing CI/PR-review gate — none of which are visible unless a session happens to be open in that repo. The daemon owns it (issue #7 single-writer) so N sessions never stampede the GitHub API. Per-repo SILENT when the viewer is not an admin (can't fix it) or a probe is indeterminate; a no-op when gh is absent/unauthenticated. NEVER mutates a repo — the on-demand /janitor-github-config-fix skill does that. Opt out by setting this to false.

daemon_github_config_audit_interval.title: Fleet GitHub-Config Audit Cadence (seconds, daemon)
daemon_github_config_audit_interval.description: Minimum seconds between the daemon's fleet GitHub-config audit passes. Default: 21600 (6 h). Each pass makes a handful of read-only gh calls per plugin repo (~13 repos); branch rulesets change rarely, so a slow cadence is correct. Only consulted when github_config_audit_enabled is true.

fleet_github_config_enabled.title: Fleet GitHub-Config Surface Enabled (per-session)
fleet_github_config_enabled.description: ON by default (TRDD-157OH2D7). The per-session fleet-github-config detector reads ONLY the daemon's findings file (one file read + a content-hash dedupe, ZERO gh calls) and emits ONE compact drift line naming the finding counts, ALWAYS ending with a pointer to /janitor-github-config-fix so the notification carries the remedy. Content-hash deduped: an unchanged finding set never re-nags; a repo getting fixed or a new gap appearing re-alerts exactly once. Silent until the daemon has written a findings file. Set false to stop surfacing the fleet findings in this project's sessions (the daemon still audits).

fleet_github_config_interval.title: Fleet GitHub-Config Surface Cadence (seconds)
fleet_github_config_interval.description: Minimum seconds between fleet-github-config surface checks. Default: 1800 (30 min). The check is near-free (one file read + hash-dedupe, no API), so it can run tight enough to surface a finding-set change promptly after the daemon's 6 h audit writes it. Only consulted when fleet_github_config_enabled is true.

guard_mode_enabled.title: Guarded Auto-Remediation Mode Enabled
guard_mode_enabled.description: Opt-in master switch for the Tier 2 guarded auto-apply path (default: false). When true, the heartbeat applies the baseline branch ruleset to the default branch automatically — force-push block, deletion block, pull-request requirement (1 approval, dismiss stale reviews, thread resolution). The baseline deliberately does NOT require linear history (it jams the many-agent merge workflow). Every other janitor remediation stays in user-invoked skills. Even with this on, the apply path no-ops unless every safety gate passes: /janitor-autofix-off NOT set, the authenticated gh viewer is repo admin, and the baseline ruleset is not already present. The Tier 1 user-invoked surface (/janitor-branch-protection-setup) works regardless of this knob.

guard_actions.title: Guarded Auto-Remediation Action Allow-List
guard_actions.description: Comma-separated list of guard actions that may run autonomously when `guard_mode_enabled` is true. Default: "branch-protection". Only listed actions are eligible; any action absent from this list is treated as opt-out even with guard_mode on. Today the only legal value is `branch-protection` — the list exists so future Tier 2 actions (e.g. `dependabot-config`, `codeowners-skeleton`) can be opted into without re-flipping `guard_mode_enabled`.

guard_min_severity.title: Guarded Auto-Remediation Minimum Severity
guard_min_severity.description: Severity threshold the underlying finding must reach before guard mode acts. Default: "critical". Valid: critical, high, medium, low. Branch-protection baseline is always critical (a default branch with no force-push block is a single-keystroke disaster), so this knob exists for future actions where the severity is variable.

guard_branch_protection_interval.title: Guard Branch-Protection Cadence (seconds)
guard_branch_protection_interval.description: Minimum seconds between guard-path branch-protection apply attempts. Default: 21600 (6 h). The applier is idempotent (returns NOOP when the baseline is already present) and runs `gh api` per attempt, so cadence is mostly a budget guard rather than a freshness knob.

pkg_manager_min_release_age_minutes.title: Package-Manager Minimum Release Age (minutes)
pkg_manager_min_release_age_minutes.description: Minimum age (in minutes) a package must reach before the pkg-manager-guard PreToolUse hook will accept it in pnpm/npm config or .npmrc / package.json#pnpm edits. Default: 7200 (~5 days) — matches the safedep.io recommendation following the 2026-05 art-template npm supply-chain compromise (~5 days between malicious publish and detection). Raising this is hardening; lowering it widens the exposure window. The hook applies this threshold to: `pnpm config set minimumReleaseAge`, `minimum-release-age` in .npmrc, and `pnpm.minimumReleaseAge` in package.json / pnpm-workspace.yaml.

pkg_manager_hook_allow_user_override.title: Package-Manager Guard Allow User Override
pkg_manager_hook_allow_user_override.description: When false (DEFAULT), the pkg-manager-guard PreToolUse hook HARD-DENIES every detected bypass (CLI flag in Bash or weakening edit in a package-manager config file) — closes issue #8. When true, the hook downgrades 'deny' to 'ask', so each block becomes a per-call confirmation. The default is false because the article's warning ("Claude will automatically use the CLI options to forcefully set the min age to 0 when he finds out that he cannot install or update something") describes precisely the failure mode an ask-style prompt cannot prevent — an agent that 'just clicks yes'. Every block is logged regardless to ~/.claude/janitor-global-state/pkg-manager-guard.log.

pkg_manager_policy_enabled.title: Package-Manager Policy Detector Enabled
pkg_manager_policy_enabled.description: When true (default), the `package-manager-policy` detector scans the project's package-manager config (.npmrc, package.json#pnpm, pnpm-workspace.yaml, .yarnrc.yml, bunfig.toml) for missing or weakened supply-chain knobs and surfaces a ONE-line drift summary listing every gap. Detection complement to the `pre-tool-pkg-guard` PreToolUse hook (the hook prevents weakening live; the detector reports pre-existing gaps). Also flags when neither `sfw` nor `safe-chain` is on PATH (no install-time malware firewall). Set false to disable scanning entirely.

pkg_manager_policy_interval.title: Package-Manager Policy Detector Cadence (seconds)
pkg_manager_policy_interval.description: Minimum seconds between `package-manager-policy` scans. Default: 21600 (6 h). Package-manager config rarely changes, and the detector content-hashes the files anyway so an unchanged-config fire costs only a few file stats; cadence mostly bounds the worst case when the firewall presence on PATH changes (install/uninstall of sfw or safe-chain).

ai_context_poisoning_enabled.title: AI-Context-Poisoning Detector Enabled
ai_context_poisoning_enabled.description: When true (default), the `ai-context-poisoning` detector scans the project's installed packages (node_modules/* + every site-packages under .venv/ / venv/ / env/) for source files that write to an agent-context file (CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, AGENTS.md, .claude/*, .mcp.json, .aider.conf.yml, etc.). This catches the supply-chain attack shape where a postinstall script silently rewrites the user's IDE-bound agent instructions on install. Read-only — never edits a package. Allowlists known config-loader packages (dotenv-cli et al.) so legitimate rewrites are silent. Set false to disable.

ai_context_poisoning_interval.title: AI-Context-Poisoning Detector Cadence (seconds)
ai_context_poisoning_interval.description: Minimum seconds between `ai-context-poisoning` scans. Default: 3600 (1 h). The detector content-hashes the relevant tree (every package.json under node_modules + every entry under each site-packages) so an unchanged-tree fire is almost free; cadence mostly bounds how quickly a newly-installed malicious package is noticed.

ai_context_poisoning_max_files.title: AI-Context-Poisoning Detector File-Scan Budget
ai_context_poisoning_max_files.description: Maximum number of source files the `ai-context-poisoning` detector will scan per heartbeat across BOTH node_modules and site-packages (default: 5000). The scan stops cleanly when the budget is exhausted so a huge node_modules tree never burns the whole heartbeat budget. Raise it for thorough repos, lower it on constrained machines.

mcp_rugpull_enabled.title: MCP Rug-Pull Detector Enabled
mcp_rugpull_enabled.description: When true (default), the `mcp-rugpull` detector fingerprints every installed MCP server's identity (transport, command, args, URL, header keys, env-var keys, local-script content hash, npx-resolved package@version) on first run and alerts on every subsequent drift. Catches the rug-pull attack shape where a previously-trusted MCP server silently rewrites its source, endpoint, or tool surface — disclosed attacks have used this to swap a `bash`-tool's spec to exfiltrate $HOME/.ssh on the next agent fire. Read-only. Set false to disable.

mcp_rugpull_interval.title: MCP Rug-Pull Detector Cadence (seconds)
mcp_rugpull_interval.description: Minimum seconds between `mcp-rugpull` scans. Default: 3600 (1 h). Server inventory changes are rare and the fingerprint diff is near-free, but a malicious update must surface fast — keep the cadence tight so a freshly-rolled rug-pull is visible within one heartbeat window.

typosquat_watcher_enabled.title: Typosquat-Watcher Detector Enabled
typosquat_watcher_enabled.description: When true (default), the `typosquat-watcher` detector walks every supported lockfile (package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, requirements.txt, uv.lock, poetry.lock) and flags any dependency name within Levenshtein distance ≤ 1 of a curated popular-package list. Catches the canonical typosquat shape (react/reactt, ethers/ethersr, web3/web33) BEFORE an advisory feed surfaces it. Read-only — never edits a lockfile. Set false to disable.

typosquat_watcher_interval.title: Typosquat-Watcher Detector Cadence (seconds)
typosquat_watcher_interval.description: Minimum seconds between `typosquat-watcher` scans. Default: 3600 (1 h). Lockfiles change rarely and the content-hash dedupe makes unchanged-tree fires almost free; cadence mostly bounds the worst-case detection window for a freshly-introduced typosquat.

typosquat_max_distance.title: Typosquat Max Levenshtein Distance
typosquat_max_distance.description: Maximum edit distance between a dependency name and a curated popular-package name that still counts as a typosquat. Default: 1 (matches every disclosed campaign — react/reactt, lodash/lodahz, web3/web33). Raise to 2 to also catch transposition typosquats like lodash/lodahs, but expect a higher false-positive rate. Hard-capped at 2 — distance ≥ 3 produces too much noise to be useful.

repo_trust_score_enabled.title: Repo Trust-Score Detector Enabled
repo_trust_score_enabled.description: When true (default), the `repo-trust-score` detector audits the current project tree for the dropper-shape pattern shared by the two known-malicious repos found in our github-monitoring study (snakebite, Pipeline-Sentinel-CI-CD-Failure-Analysis). Combines five signals into a trust-deficit score: suspicious binaries in promo dirs (image/, samples/, etc.), README download-funnel language pointing at a local binary, SEO-keyword stuffing in README paragraphs, camouflage ratio (heavy README vs thin source), and missing essentials (no CI / tests / LICENSE). Read-only — never edits a file. Set false to disable.

repo_trust_score_interval.title: Repo Trust-Score Detector Cadence (seconds)
repo_trust_score_interval.description: Minimum seconds between `repo-trust-score` scans. Default: 21600 (6 h). The relevant signals (README content, binary inventory) change slowly; content-hash dedupe makes unchanged-tree fires almost free.

pre_bash_safety_enabled.title: Pre-Bash-Safety Hook Enabled (OPT-IN)
pre_bash_safety_enabled.description: When true, the `pre-bash-safety` PreToolUse hook fires on every Bash tool call and DENIES (or asks, with override) commands matching the two compositional-attack classes the static regex tier cannot catch: (1) source+sink exfil chains where `cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa` is piped/chained into `curl -X POST` / `nc` / a known exfil sink; (2) surgical writes to sensitive paths (.git/hooks/*, ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, ~/.aws/credentials, .github/workflows/*.yml). OPT-IN by default (false) because some legitimate workflows touch these paths; turn it on once you've audited your repo's normal shell usage.

pre_bash_safety_allow_override.title: Pre-Bash-Safety Allow-Override Mode
pre_bash_safety_allow_override.description: When true, the `pre-bash-safety` hook returns `permissionDecision: ask` instead of `deny` for every blocked call — so the user can confirm individual legitimate commands per call. Default: false (hard deny).

memory_guard_enabled.title: Tier-1 OOM Memory-Guard Enabled
memory_guard_enabled.description: When true (default), the global daemon's `memory-guard` task checks system free memory every memory_guard_interval seconds; under real pressure (free below memory_guard_min_free_mb) it snapshots the process table to a file and kills the single largest-RSS JANITOR-OWNED runaway (a stuck `claude plugin marketplace update`, an orphaned rotator/reauth/capture subprocess older than the runaway age gate). Tier-1 only: an explicit signature allowlist plus a hard claude-session rejection means interactive `claude` sessions, the daemon itself, and every system process are never candidates by construction; at most one kill per beat; every kill is logged with full cmdline, RSS, age, and the triggering free-memory reading. Tier 2 (killing non-janitor processes) is deliberately NOT implemented. Part of the resilient-daemon design (TRDD-7100178d Pillar 4, Decision 1).

memory_guard_min_free_mb.title: Memory-Guard Free-Memory Floor (MB)
memory_guard_min_free_mb.description: System free memory (MB) below which the daemon's memory-guard starts looking for a janitor-owned runaway to kill. Default: 1024. An unknown reading is always a no-op (the guard never kills on missing data).

context_watchdog_enabled.title: Context-Size Runaway Guard Enabled
context_watchdog_enabled.description: When true (DEFAULT), the `pre-tool-context-usage` PreToolUse hook fires on every tool call and guards the per-turn CONTEXT-SIZE token bleed — two-tiered. ADVISORY (at/above context_compact_suggest_pct): injects the % + a /janitor-compact-context nudge via additionalContext, without altering the tool's permission flow. ENFORCEMENT (at/above context_hardstop_pct, gated by context_autocompact_enabled): queues a compaction on this pane and DENIES the tool call so the turn ends cleanly for /compact, after which post-compact-resume continues the work at a reduced context. Occupancy is read from the statusline snapshot at <project>/.claude/janitor/context-usage.<session>.json, or (no statusline) falls back to the transcript's latest assistant input+cache occupancy (token_meter.latest_context_size) over context_window_tokens. Every path FAILS OPEN: a read error or no automatable terminal degrades to the advisory, never a stuck deny. DEFAULT-ON because the per-turn context bleed it prevents cost the user a month of tokens (every turn re-reads the WHOLE context, so a session near the 1M cap burns ~its size in tokens per turn); set false to disable both tiers, or context_autocompact_enabled=false to keep only the advisory. Part of the context watchdog (TRDD-31095269, TRDD-SMZFJVZ3); pairs with the post-compact-resume PostCompact hook and the /janitor-compact-context skill.

context_compact_suggest_pct.title: Context-Size Guard - Advisory (Warn) Threshold (%)
context_compact_suggest_pct.description: Context-window usage % at or above which the watchdog's PreToolUse hook appends a suggestion to run /janitor-compact-context. Default 60 — leaves ~40% headroom so /compact can still run (wait too long, e.g. to ~999k on the 1M window, and /compact itself fails, forcing a total-loss /clear). This is the soft WARN level; the hard ENFORCE level is context_hardstop_pct. Only consulted when context_watchdog_enabled is true.

context_hardstop_pct.title: Context-Size Guard - Enforcement (Hard-Stop) Threshold (%)
context_hardstop_pct.description: Context-window usage % at or above which the guard's ENFORCEMENT tier queues a compaction on this session's pane and DENIES the in-flight tool call so the turn ends cleanly for /compact (post-compact-resume then continues at a reduced context). Default 85 - high enough to be rare, low enough that /compact still succeeds. Gated by context_autocompact_enabled (set that false to keep only the advisory nudge). The deny fires at most once per compaction episode (180s dedupe) and ONLY when a compaction can actually be queued (an automatable iTerm/tmux pane); with no such terminal, or on any error, it degrades to the advisory - never a stuck deny. Set 0 to disable enforcement by threshold. Only consulted when context_watchdog_enabled is true.

context_autocompact_enabled.title: Context-Size Guard - Auto-Compact Enforcement Enabled
context_autocompact_enabled.description: When true (DEFAULT), the guard's ENFORCEMENT tier is active: at or above context_hardstop_pct it auto-queues /compact on this pane and denies the tool call to end the turn (auto-resumed afterward). When false, the guard is advisory-only - it still injects the context % and the /janitor-compact-context nudge at context_compact_suggest_pct, but NEVER denies a tool call (the agent decides when to compact). Set false if you do not want the guard to ever interrupt a turn. Only consulted when context_watchdog_enabled is true.

context_window_tokens.title: Context-Size Guard - Fallback Window (tokens)
context_window_tokens.description: The context-window size (in tokens) the guard uses to compute the usage % when reading occupancy from the TRANSCRIPT fallback (no statusline snapshot present). Default 1000000 (the 1M window). When the statusline snapshot is available it carries the real window and this value is ignored. Set to match your model's actual context window if you run a non-1M window and rely on the transcript fallback. Only consulted when context_watchdog_enabled is true.

postcompact_push_enabled.title: Post-Compact Resume Push Enabled
postcompact_push_enabled.description: ON by default (TRDD-HI0BGQGJ). After a context compaction the `post-compact-resume` hook records WHAT to resume in a flag, but the WAKE was pull-only: only the next heartbeat cron fire reads that flag, and on an idle session the cron has demoted to the SLOW ~30-min floor — so nothing was written for up to 30 minutes (the exact 'agent stalled after compaction' failure). When true, the hook ALSO fires a detached `resume_trigger.py` that types /janitor-resume into this session's own iTerm/tmux pane, so the resume runs in seconds instead of waiting for the slow cron. Gated to UNATTENDED sessions only (see postcompact_push_attended_grace_s): a recently-active user is left alone and resumed by the cron path as before, so keystrokes are never typed into a live input line. Fully fail-safe — a non-automatable terminal (plain Terminal.app / VS Code / CI) degrades to the cron path with no regression, and any push fault never affects the compaction. Set to false to opt OUT and keep only the cron-driven resume.

postcompact_push_attended_grace_s.title: Post-Compact Resume Push - Attended Grace (seconds)
postcompact_push_attended_grace_s.description: Seconds of recency that count a session as ATTENDED for the post-compact resume push (default 180). If a GENUINE user prompt (the cross-plugin user-presence breadcrumb's last_user_input_epoch, bumped only by real input — never by a cron heartbeat) landed within this window, the push is SKIPPED and the session is resumed by the normal cron path instead, so the janitor never types /janitor-resume into a live input line. A larger value is more conservative (treats the user as present for longer — fewer pushes); a smaller value pushes sooner after the last keystroke. Only consulted when postcompact_push_enabled is true.

cold_cache_compact_enabled.title: Cold-Cache Auto-Compact on Resume Enabled
cold_cache_compact_enabled.description: ON by default (TRDD-EUWIHP0G). After a >1h stop (a rate limit; the user exits and relaunches later; a logout/login), the 1h prompt-cache TTL has expired, so the FIRST resumed turn re-writes the WHOLE context as a cache-creation (~600k tokens on average, billed ~1.25×), burning a large chunk of the 5h window. When true, the janitor self-fires /compact on resume whenever a LARGE context comes back cold — at SessionStart (source startup/resume, context >= cold_cache_compact_min_context_tokens) and on the heartbeat rate-limit-clear path (the gap outlived the cache TTL AND the context is large). It CANNOT avoid that immediate cold write (any first turn pays it), but it shrinks the context to ~50k so the REST of the window — and every FUTURE cold resume — runs cheap instead of dragging ~600k forward on every turn. The compaction is SOFT (the resumed REPL is idle, so nothing is interrupted) and the resume is preserved: post-compact-resume records the directive and continues the prior task after compaction. Fully fail-safe — a non-automatable terminal (plain Terminal.app / VS Code / CI) or any fault degrades to the normal resume with no regression. Set to false to opt OUT.

cold_cache_compact_min_context_tokens.title: Cold-Cache Auto-Compact - Minimum Context (tokens)
cold_cache_compact_min_context_tokens.description: The resumed-context size (input + cache_read + cache_creation of the last assistant turn) at or above which the cold-cache auto-compact fires (default 270000). Below this the context is small enough that a cold re-write is cheap and compacting it saves nothing (and is lossy), so the trigger is a no-op — a fresh/empty session therefore never trips it. Raise it to compact only very large contexts; lower it to compact more eagerly. Only consulted when cold_cache_compact_enabled is true.

cold_cache_compact_min_idle_seconds.title: Cold-Cache Auto-Compact - Minimum Idle (seconds)
cold_cache_compact_min_idle_seconds.description: How long an IN-SESSION gap must last before the heartbeat rate-limit path treats the prompt cache as COLD and eligible for auto-compact (default 3600 — the 1h prompt-cache TTL). Below this the cache is still warm, so compacting would just waste a write; the branch stays silent and emits the normal resume cue. This gate applies ONLY to the heartbeat rate-limit path — the SessionStart path has no idle gate (a fresh process loading a large context is cold by construction). Only consulted when cold_cache_compact_enabled is true.

cold_cache_compact_cooldown_seconds.title: Cold-Cache Auto-Compact - Cooldown (seconds)
cold_cache_compact_cooldown_seconds.description: Seconds after a cold-cache compact fires during which another one is suppressed (default 600), shared by the SessionStart and heartbeat trigger points via a single stamp. This prevents a second, redundant /compact from being queued before the first one actually lands (compaction is not instantaneous). Large enough to cover the window between firing /compact and the compaction completing; a value below the real compaction latency risks a double-fire. Only consulted when cold_cache_compact_enabled is true.

proactive_idle_compact_enabled.title: Proactive Idle Auto-Compact Enabled
proactive_idle_compact_enabled.description: ON by default (TRDD-D3PROACT). The cold-cache paths above are REACTIVE — they shrink a large context only AFTER a cold fire already paid the ~2× cache-creation write, because a cron fire re-reads the whole transcript BEFORE the janitor can act (the burn is unavoidable on that fire). This is the PREVENTIVE path: on a heartbeat where the session is genuinely idle (the user has not typed in this pane for >=5 min AND there is no pending resume / keep-going / directive / in-flight agent) AND the context is large (>= cold_cache_compact_min_context_tokens), it self-fires a SOFT /compact NOW — during a cheap WARM fire — so the context is already ~50k when the next cold event (a >1h working turn, a rate limit, a restart) strikes. It is the only path that PREVENTS the cold burn rather than mitigating it after the fact. Compaction is lossy, so the idle + absent-user gates ensure it never fires out from under active work, and the resume is preserved (post-compact-resume records the directive and continues the prior task). It terminates because it also requires that a compaction could reclaim at least proactive_idle_compact_min_gain_tokens above this session's learned post-compaction floor — NOT because 'the context is small afterwards' (measured false: a real compaction here went 343,007 -> 308,644, above the threshold, which a size-only gate could never close). Fail-safe: a non-automatable terminal or any fault degrades to no compact with no regression. Requires cold_cache_compact_enabled; set this to false to keep only the reactive backstops.

proactive_idle_compact_min_gain_tokens.title: Proactive Idle Auto-Compact Minimum Reclaimable Tokens
proactive_idle_compact_min_gain_tokens.description: How many tokens a compaction must be able to RECLAIM before the proactive idle path fires one (default 150000). A compaction can only reclaim what sits ABOVE this session's post-compaction floor — the context it leaves behind, which on a heavy install is dominated by the base that reloads every time (CLAUDE.md + plugins + rules + skills + MCP schemas + the summary) and cannot be compacted away. The janitor learns that floor by observing the context right after each compaction. This is the gate that makes the trigger TERMINATE: at the floor there is nothing left to reclaim, so it goes silent until real new work accumulates. Without it, an install whose floor sits above cold_cache_compact_min_context_tokens would compact every cooldown forever, destroying context each time (measured in the janitor's own repo 2026-07-17: 343,007 -> 308,644 against a 270,000 threshold). Raise it to compact less often, lower it to compact more eagerly; 0 disables the gate and is NOT recommended unless you have verified your floor is below the threshold.

memory_autorecall.title: Automatic Memory Recall on Prompt
memory_autorecall.description: ON by default (issue #45). The `on-prompt-submit-autorecall` UserPromptSubmit hook runs `memgrep recall` over ALL THREE memory scopes — LOCAL (~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/), PROJECT (<git-root>/.claude/project/memory/) and USER (the janitor's plugin-data memory dir) — on every ordinary user prompt, and injects the top notes into the agent context via additionalContext, so the agent is automatically reminded of relevant prior notes ('have we hit this before?') without calling recall by hand. Recall is AUTOMATIC because discipline-only recall demonstrably fails: a memory-aware agent still re-derived a framework it had itself authored, because it did not recall first. It searches ONLY agent-visible notes: the private user-mem store (.../memory/user-mem/) is structurally excluded (recall is handed explicit file paths, never the dir, and only walks directories), so a private user memory is never surfaced. Cron [janitor-…] prompts, slash commands and sub-threshold prompts ('yes', 'do it') are skipped; a missing memgrep binary, an empty corpus, or any error is a silent no-op (never blocks or crashes the turn). Set to false to opt OUT. Part of the memory system (issues #16/#45); pairs with the markdown-memory-recall rule and the janitor-memory-recall/janitor-memory-write skills.

memory_recall_invite.title: Recall Invite on Prompt
memory_recall_invite.description: ON by default (TRDD-7B1THXTB). On every non-trivial user prompt the autorecall hook ALSO injects a one-line INVITATION for the agent to run its own `memgrep recall` with keywords IT derives — on a recall hit the invite is appended after the surfaced notes; on a miss it is injected alone. The invite never names or suggests a specific memory (that stays the agent's job); it exists because auto-surfacing ranks the RAW prompt and can miss the note that matters — the motivating failure re-hit a trap already documented in the corpus because nothing prompted a search. Kept to one line (it rides every prompt). Set to false to restore silence on a recall miss; setting memory_autorecall to false disables the whole hook, invite included.

memory_breadcrumb.title: Session-Start Memory Breadcrumb
memory_breadcrumb.description: ON by default. At session start the janitor prints ONE line naming how many memory notes each scope holds (LOCAL + PROJECT + USER) and the `memgrep overview <dir>` entry point — the missing 'what do I have?' breadcrumb (janitor#62 gaps 2+3). Without it the 3-scope wikimem is invisible to a fresh session unless the agent already knows memgrep: autorecall only pushes a note when a prompt happens to match it. The line carries COUNTS ONLY, never note content, so an untrusted PROJECT-scope page (git input from any contributor) cannot inject text into the session prefix through this surface. Silent when every scope is empty, so an install with no memory corpus pays nothing. Set to false to opt out.

post_edit_safety_enabled.title: Post-Edit-Safety Hook Enabled (OPT-IN)
post_edit_safety_enabled.description: When true, the `post-edit-safety` PostToolUse hook fires AFTER every Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit and surfaces an additionalContext warning when the write landed at a sensitive path (.git/hooks/*, ~/.ssh/*, ~/.aws/*, .github/workflows/*, ~/.bashrc, /etc/*) OR contains a sensitive payload (eval+base64 decode, curl|sh, /dev/tcp reverse-shell, ssh-rsa being written). Catches the 'model was conned into WRITING attack code' class that the pre-bash hook (which catches EXECUTION) does not. OPT-IN by default (false). From the narthex sweep-A.

post_mcp_sanitizer_enabled.title: Post-MCP-Response Sanitiser Hook Enabled
post_mcp_sanitizer_enabled.description: ON by default. The `post-mcp-response-sanitizer` PostToolUse hook fires AFTER every mcp__* tool call and, on a strong injection signal, STRIPS covert invisible/bidi unicode and replaces the payload via updatedToolOutput (a homoglyph-only weak signal warns instead of replacing). It detects prompt-injection shapes: invisible unicode (zero-width / bidi override), NFKC homoglyph diffs (a Cyrillic look-alike substituted for a Latin letter, etc.), and jailbreak phrasing (instruction-override openers, role-reassignment openers, fake system-tag and frame-break markers). It defaults ON because third-party MCP servers can return attacker-controlled web content (scraped pages, issue bodies) that lands directly in the model's context — protection must not depend on a user remembering to enable it. Set to false to opt out; set post_mcp_sanitizer_strip=false for warn-only. From the narthex sweep-A.

historical_cache_scan_enabled.title: Historical-Cache-Scan Detector Enabled
historical_cache_scan_enabled.description: When true (default), the `historical-cache-scan` detector walks every machine-wide npm/pnpm/yarn cache + every global node_modules path (nvm/fnm/volta/system) checking whether any known-malicious package@version listed in `.janitor/incidents.txt` was ever fetched on this machine. Crucial because removing the bad version from package.json is not enough — `npm install` from the same cache can silently re-fetch. The user maintains `.janitor/incidents.txt` (one `name@version` per line) from OSV.dev MAL-* advisories that supply-chain-watcher surfaces. Read-only — never modifies a cache. Set false to disable. From npm-chainsaw sweep-A.

historical_cache_scan_interval.title: Historical-Cache-Scan Detector Cadence (seconds)
historical_cache_scan_interval.description: Minimum seconds between `historical-cache-scan` scans. Default: 21600 (6 h). Incident lists change rarely and the detector content-hashes the input list + cache-dir inventory, so unchanged-state fires return almost immediately; the cadence mostly bounds how quickly a freshly-added OSV MAL-* surfaces a hit.

historical_cache_max_files.title: Historical-Cache-Scan File-Walk Budget
historical_cache_max_files.description: Maximum number of files the `historical-cache-scan` detector walks per heartbeat across all caches + global node_modules paths combined (default: 50000). The scan stops cleanly when the budget is exhausted so a huge nvm-with-N-node-versions tree never burns the whole heartbeat budget. Raise it on thoroughly-stocked machines; lower it on tightly-constrained ones.

binary_magic_scanner_enabled.title: Binary Magic-Byte Scanner Enabled
binary_magic_scanner_enabled.description: When true (default), the `binary-magic-scanner` detector walks `.github/`, `scripts/`, `docs/`, `tests/`, `examples/`, `image*/`, `download*/`, `release*/` and surfaces any file whose first 8 bytes match an ELF / PE / Mach-O / Java-class / Wasm / Zip magic-byte signature. Catches the dropper-shape malware corpus (snakebite, Pipeline-Sentinel, Sentinel-main-3) from a different angle than `repo-trust-score`. Read-only — never modifies a file. Set false to disable.

binary_magic_interval.title: Binary Magic-Byte Scanner Cadence (seconds)
binary_magic_interval.description: Minimum seconds between `binary-magic-scanner` scans. Default: 21600 (6 h). Content-hash dedupe makes unchanged-tree fires near-free; cadence mostly bounds how quickly a newly-introduced binary blob surfaces.

binary_magic_max_files.title: Binary Magic-Byte Scanner File Budget
binary_magic_max_files.description: Maximum number of files the `binary-magic-scanner` reads per heartbeat (default: 5000). The scan stops cleanly when the budget is exhausted.

supply_chain_fingerprints_enabled.title: Supply-Chain-Fingerprints Detector Enabled
supply_chain_fingerprints_enabled.description: When true (default), the `supply-chain-fingerprints` heartbeat detector runs six aggregated sub-checks: import-cluster pairing in setup.py + package.json scripts (obfuscation + network/exec clusters), maintainer-join-vs-publish gap on locked deps, wheel-absence heuristic for PyPI deps, fresh-publisher first-release shape, HTTP 451 npm security-hold surfacing, ghost-publisher reawake (long-quiet → sudden republish). Default cadence 6h; live registry calls are opt-in via the per-sub-check flags inside the detector. Read-only — never modifies a file. Set false to disable.

supply_chain_fingerprints_interval.title: Supply-Chain-Fingerprints Detector Cadence (seconds)
supply_chain_fingerprints_interval.description: Minimum seconds between `supply-chain-fingerprints` runs. Default: 21600 (6 h).

provenance_audit_enabled.title: Provenance-Audit Detector Enabled
provenance_audit_enabled.description: When true (default), the `provenance-audit` detector scans the project's release infrastructure for SBOM presence, cosign-verify steps, npm provenance flag, in-toto attestation chain, SLSA-level floor, and XZ-style release-vs-git divergence. Read-only — never modifies a file. Set false to disable.

provenance_audit_interval.title: Provenance-Audit Detector Cadence (seconds)
provenance_audit_interval.description: Minimum seconds between `provenance-audit` runs. Default: 21600 (6 h). Release infrastructure changes rarely; content-hash dedupe keeps unchanged-tree fires near-free.

janitor_self_integrity_enabled.title: Janitor Self-Integrity Detector Enabled (OPT-IN)
janitor_self_integrity_enabled.description: When true, the `janitor-self-integrity` detector verifies the janitor's own scripts/ + skills/ + CLAUDE.md against a checked-in SHA-256 manifest, and maintains an HMAC-chained append-only audit log of every heartbeat fire. OPT-IN by default (false) because the verifier produces a drift line on EVERY change to the janitor's own files — useful for the maintainer, noisy for normal users. Flip to true if you want tamper-evidence on the janitor itself.

janitor_self_integrity_interval.title: Janitor Self-Integrity Detector Cadence (seconds)
janitor_self_integrity_interval.description: Minimum seconds between `janitor-self-integrity` scans. Default: 21600 (6 h).

tickets_enabled.title: Support-Ticket Incident Queue
tickets_enabled.description: When true (DEFAULT), the janitor turns a detected incident into a support ticket and repairs it (TRDD-CGYMUKO6). HARNESS incidents — its OWN machinery (a corrupt memgrep index, a failed migration, a crash-looping daemon) — open and dispatch a repair agent automatically. PROJECT incidents — YOUR code, repo, workflows — are only ever PROPOSED: the janitor writes a proposal TRDD and recommends `/janitor-support-open-ticket TRDD-<id>`; nothing is dispatched and nothing in your repo is touched until you run it. Set false to disable the queue entirely (detectors keep detecting; they just stop opening tickets).

tickets_per_heartbeat.title: Ticket Dispatches per Heartbeat
tickets_per_heartbeat.description: Maximum repair agents the scheduler may dispatch on ONE heartbeat fire. Default: 2. A cap, not a target — an unbounded repair queue is one bug away from being a token fire.

tickets_per_day.title: Ticket Dispatches per Rolling 24h
tickets_per_day.description: Maximum repair agents dispatched in any rolling 24-hour window. Default: 20. The backstop against a repair that keeps failing and keeps being retried.

ticket_max_attempts.title: Ticket Max Attempts
ticket_max_attempts.description: How many times a ticket may be worked before it becomes `needs_human` and is surfaced on every heartbeat until a person deals with it. Default: 3. It is NEVER silently dropped — a silent give-up is indistinguishable from a fix.

ticket_backoff_s.title: Ticket Retry Backoff (seconds)
ticket_backoff_s.description: How long a failed ticket waits before it may be dispatched again. Default: 1800 (30 min).

ticket_stale_s.title: Ticket Stale Reclaim (seconds)
ticket_stale_s.description: How long a dispatched ticket may sit with no progress before its agent is presumed DEAD and the ticket is reclaimed for another attempt. Default: 3600 (1 h). Without this, an agent killed mid-work (a rate-limit cap will do it) strands its ticket forever and the queue quietly stops.

ticket_dispatch_interval.title: Ticket Scheduler Cadence (seconds)
ticket_dispatch_interval.description: Minimum seconds between `ticket-dispatch` runs. Default: 300 (every heartbeat) — an empty queue costs a directory glob that finds nothing, and a critical incident should not wait out a long cadence.

memgrep_health_interval.title: Memgrep Index-Health Cadence (seconds)
memgrep_health_interval.description: Minimum seconds between `memgrep-index-health` probes of each memory scope's search index. Default: 1800 (30 min). A failure must RECUR before it becomes a ticket.
